headline_marked: 71-run win: [[Bangladesh crush Indonesia]] in Asia Cup opener
headline: 71-run win: Bangladesh crush Indonesia in Asia Cup opener
summary: The Tigresses dominated their first match with a strong batting performance and a lethal bowling attack, bundling Indonesia out for just 58.
details: Bangladesh started their Asia Cup campaign with a dominant 71-run victory over Indonesia at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Monday.
Batting first, Bangladesh posted a respectable total of 129/8, with Sobhana Mostary scoring 40 and Shorna Akter contributing an unbeaten 31.
The bowling unit then took control, with Nahida Akter claiming 3/15 and Marufa Akter taking 2/6, restricting Indonesia to just 58 runs.
Despite the win, captain Nigar Sultana Joty urged her team to rectify mistakes in bowling areas to prepare for their next challenge.
The Tigresses will face reigning champions Sri Lanka on Sunday at the same venue, a match Joty describes as crucial for their goal of topping the group.
Indonesia captain Nanda Sakarini praised her bowlers' efforts but admitted the team needs to be more ruthless to compete against larger teams.
caption:
A dominant start for the Tigresses! 🇧🇩

Bangladesh crushed Indonesia by 71 runs in their Asia Cup opener.

Bangladesh started their Asia Cup campaign with a dominant 71-run victory over Indonesia at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium on Monday.

Batting first, Bangladesh posted a respectable total of 129/8, with Sobhana Mostary scoring 40 and Shorna Akter contributing an unbeaten 31.

The bowling unit then took control, with Nahida Akter claiming 3/15 and Marufa Akter taking 2/6, restricting Indonesia to just 58 runs.

Despite the win, captain Nigar Sultana Joty urged her team to rectify mistakes in bowling areas to prepare for their next challenge.

The Tigresses will face reigning champions Sri Lanka on Sunday at the same venue, a match Joty describes as crucial for their goal of topping the group.

Indonesia captain Nanda Sakarini praised her bowlers' efforts but admitted the team needs to be more ruthless to compete against larger teams.
